8.3.3 Coley Creek Site
The upper reservoir of the Coley Creek site would be located on Coley Creek, a tributary of the Thompson River (Figure 8-5). This site is located in Transylvania County, North Carolina, and Oconee County, South Carolina, about 4.5 miles south of Oakland, North Carolina, and about 2.5 miles northeast of the Bad Creek site. The Coley Creek site is located within Nantahala National Forest and Sumter National Forest.
The reservoir would contain 49,000 acre-feet of usable storage between water surface elevation 2,010 and 1,880 feet. At maximum water level elevation 2,010 feet, the reservoir would have a surface area of about 400 acres. Jocassee Reservoir would be used as the lower reservoir. The upper reservoir would be formed by a main dam with a maximum height of about 400 feet and a crest length of about 4,000 feet, an auxiliary dam about 210 feet high and 1,300 feet long at the crest, a saddle dike about 20 feet high and 1,000 feet long at the crest, and a saddle dike about 10 feet high. The power tunnel would be about 7,700 feet long and would have a diameter of 34 feet. An underground powerhouse would be constructed containing 4 units rated at 250 MW capacity each.
8.3.3.1 Flora
A specific vegetative description of the Coley Creek alternative site is not available, but the vegetation types should be essentially the same as those described in Subsection 2.2.1. The occurrence of rare plants as described in Subsection 2.2.3 is probable in this area.
The environmental impacts should be similar in kind to those discussed for the proposed Bad Creek site in Subsections 3.1.2 and 3.2.2. About 400 acres of riverbank shrub thicket, disturbed floodplain forest, mixed mesophytic forest, and mixed oak-hickory forest would be inundated. The associated wildlife habitat and some wildlife, timber, and watershed values of this forested area would be lost.
